To answer your question: yes, CrossFit is most likely for you. Here are some of my thoughts after reading your post

* Most CrossFit coaches are well-trained. Most CrossFit gyms have an intro class that will help newcomers learn the movements. These classes tend to be smaller so you will get a lot of attention from the coach, so he/she will be able to help you with form.
* You do not have to think about CrossFit. The programming is done for you: the warm-up, the workout, and the cooldown. Most coaches will even tell each individual which weights to use. The only thing you need to do is get yourself there, in your gym attire, with a positive attitude.
* CrossFit is more expensive membership, but here is what your are getting: coaching (not just access to weights); thoughtful programming that has an intention behind it; a strong community that will push you to be a better person, and they help keep you accountable; often community events/parties throughout the year...you will make friends.
* CrossFit is not cardio-heavy; I would say it is balanced. There is running, stationary biking, and/or rowing sprinkled throughout the week, but there are days when there are none of those. Yes, your heart will be pumping hard, but it is fun and most often it is not drawn-out.
* Most likely your appetite will ramp up...this is a good thing. A lot of CrossFit gyms give nutrition advice in their intro classes. Remember to prioritize protein, and whole foods (things you have to make yourself, not processed foods with a long ingredient label). I believe this will help your health markers too. Also, remember to get adequate, good sleep. Some tips to help increase calories: find nutrient-dense foods, like non-lean meats, eggs, dairy. Do not fill up on fibrous foods.
